Apple is reported to have significantly increased orders for vapor chambers, suggesting this cooling technology may play a more important role in its future hardware product lineup. Details below.

Apple bets big on vapor chamber cooling technology

Weibo tipster Fixed Focus Digital claimed Apple has "significantly increased its overall vapor chamber order volume," noting this "may be in preparation for enhanced cooling for the first foldable iPhone and the next-generation twentieth anniversary model."

Apple first introduced vapor chamber cooling technology on the iPhone 17 Pro, a change that helped address thermal issues that had plagued previous models.

A vapor chamber works by evaporating a small amount of liquid near the heat source, condensing it at a cooler spot to disperse heat across a larger surface, then letting the liquid return to repeat the cycle.

You can see the entire process in action in this fantastic video from Know Art:

Although the Weibo post speculated Apple's move is preparation for the iPhone Ultra and the twentieth anniversary iPhone expected in 2027, timing makes it more reasonable for this year's lineup to adopt the new cooling solution.

Apple is reportedly asking suppliers to prepare around 10 million foldable iPhones, above the earlier target of 7 to 8 million, as well as approximately 70 million iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units. All three models are expected to feature vapor chamber cooling.

The order increase comes amid reports that Apple has resolved earlier hinge and production yield issues, clearing the way for higher production targets ahead of the September launch.
